title: Pumpkin Purchase
statementMd:
You are in charge of buying a pumpkin to carve into a jack-o'-lantern for your suite's Halloween decorations! After performing extensive research at the nearby supermarket, you've realized that the supermarket generally charges more for larger pumpkins, but the relationship is complicated: you've fit a cubic curve relating price p𝑝 of the pumpkin to its volume:

V(p)=a0p3+a1p2+a2p+a3

𝑉(𝑝)=𝑎0𝑝3+𝑎1𝑝2+𝑎2𝑝+𝑎3

for some positive constants ai you've calculated from the data.

A good-looking jack-o'-lantern must be carved from a pumpkin of volume at least VT. Given VT, what's the cheapest price you'll have to pay to acquire a sufficiently-large pumpkin?

## Input

The only line of input contains five space-separated real numbers VT, a0, a1, a2, and a3. These numbers might be expressed in scientific notation (see sample inputs) and are all in the range [10−9,109].

## Output

Print the smallest value of p for which V(p)≥VT. Your answer will be judged correct if it differs from the judge's solution by absolute or relative error at most 10−6.

## Note

Hint: in order to satisfy the above error bound, be sure to print many digits of p (at least 8).

For example, if your answer is stored in `ans`:

- Java: System.out.printf("%.10f%n", ans);
- C++: cout << fixed << setprecision(10) << ans << '\n'; (include `<iomanip>`)
- Python: print(f"{ans:.10f}")
